clue.text: Getting sentimental over snooker shot in The Crucible

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits over (above) the second

parts.note: someone going soft with emotion is said to be melting
a pot is a shot that sinks a ball in snooker

explanation.surface: A snooker player gets emotional after a winning shot at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crucible in Sheffield is where the World Snooker Championship is played, which is why the surface feels so natural; here the word is just a vessel for melting and mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A crucible is a vessel where metals are fused together, the literal sense of the mixing pot phrase.

clue.text: Form of tribute from the war, originally

indicators.note: taken as 'in an original way', the letters of the words are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A memorial tribute that began with the war, such as a poppy for the fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' looks like it means first letters, but here it signals rearranging all of THE WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of flowers is laid at a grave or memorial as a mark of respect.

clue.text: Musical offering from old sailor over in old port

indicators.note: the first group of letters is placed inside the second group

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'over' turns the letters upward, so they are read backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A piece of music presented by a former seaman back in an ancient harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns O + TAR into RATO, which goes inside O + RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: An extended choral work on a sacred theme, performed as a concert piece.

clue.text: Embrace or fondle, perhaps?

indicators.note: the question 'or fondle, perhaps?' hints that those letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a hug might really be groping.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap someone in your arms is to hug or encircle them.

clue.text: Special rite in classical language mostly for educated people

indicators.note: the rearranged word is placed inside the shortened language
most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Latin is the classical language of ancient Rome

indicators.note: something special is made out of the ordinary, so the letters of the word rite are reworked

explanation.surface: A special Latin ceremony laid on for the intelligentsia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' rearranges RITE into ITER, which goes inside LATI ('mostly' drops the last letter of LATIN).
explanation.definitionFit: The well-read class, people of letters and learning.

clue.text: Olympian given hard time

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An Olympic athlete is given a rough time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' suggests an athlete, but it means a god living on Mount Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen of the Greek gods, wife of Zeus, dwelt on Mount Olympus.

clue.text: Barrier constructed by Welsh, English and Irish

explanation.surface: A dam built jointly by workers from Wales, England and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A low dam built across a river to control its flow.

clue.text: Think again about playing team in Costa Rica

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the playing team is put inside the country code

parts.note: CR is the international vehicle code for Costa Rica
a player on the field is on
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A football squad on tour in Central America has second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks part of the definition but supplies RE; CR is the international vehicle code for Costa Rica, and 'in' puts ON + SIDE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh a decision a second time, perhaps changing your mind.

clue.text: Focus on former striker

parts.note: the centre is the focus or middle point
'on' as in 'go on' means forward

explanation.surface: Attention turns to a footballer who used to lead the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The striker is the attacking footballer; the term is old-fashioned, hence 'former'.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional name for the central attacking player in football, now usually called a striker.

clue.text: Characteristic seen in nurse leading to distress

indicators.note: the trait is spotted sitting inside the nurse abbreviation

parts.note: SEN stood for State Enrolled Nurse in Britain
a trait is a characteristic

explanation.surface: A personal quirk in a nurse ends up causing anguish.
explanation.walkthrough: SEN (State Enrolled Nurse) was a British nursing grade.
explanation.definitionFit: To straiten someone is to put them in difficulty or hardship, as in straitened circumstances.

clue.text: A thoroughfare like Tottenham Court Road?

parts.note: a means one
a way is a road or route

explanation.surface: A London street held up as an example of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Court Road, in central London, was long a single-direction street; the question mark flags definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic on such a street may travel in only a single direction.

clue.text: Part of plant — a different one, not requiring oxygen

indicators.note: doing without something means it is left out of the word

parts.note: another means a different one
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A botanist notes that a different plant part can do without oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollen-bearing tip of a flower's stamen.

clue.text: Domestic feature apt to make Arabia extremely torrid?

indicators.note: the letters are put together to make something new
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A household heater that is liable to make the Arabian desert scorching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of Arabia, A and A, and 'make' rearranges them with TORRID.
explanation.definitionFit: A heater fixed to the wall of a home, warming the room.

clue.text: Expert in front of Money section is mistaken

indicators.note: taken the wrong way, so the letters are put into a new order
the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A financial pundit gets the money pages wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; IN, M (from 'front of Money') and SECTION are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing everything, the ultimate in expertise.

clue.text: Repetitious style of pirate's shoulder accessory?

indicators.note: the style of a thing follows the thing itself

parts.note: a pirate traditionally carries a parrot on his shoulder
a fashion is a style

explanation.surface: A costume note about the bird perched on a pirate's shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating words mechanically without understanding, the way a talking bird mimics speech.

clue.text: Around church outside house woodwind instrument resounded

annotationWithheld.why: Around church outside house woodwind instrument resounded: REED holds RE..ED round ECHO, but no reading of 'Around church outside house' gives ECHO (CE outside HO gives CHOE)
annotationWithheld.clue: Around church outside house woodwind instrument resounded

clue.text: In distress, bringing in doctor with yellow turned-up hat

indicators.note: the doctor's letters are brought inside the word for distress

parts.note: sore here means distressed or aggrieved
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are turned upward, reading backwards

parts.note: or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: Someone upset calls a doctor about a yellow hat with an upturned brim.
explanation.walkthrough: SORE with MB inside makes SOMBRE; 'turned-up' reverses OR into RO.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Stone boring instrument used to make flag

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight
a reamer is a tool for enlarging holes

explanation.surface: A mason uses a drill on stone to make a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is stone, the British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow pennant or ribbon flown from a mast.

clue.text: Protest as odd drink's knocked over

indicators.note: in a down clue, upended letters read backwards

parts.note: rum means odd or strange in British slang
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a strange drink has been spilled.
explanation.walkthrough: Both RUMs are turned round together by 'knocked over'.
explanation.definitionFit: A muttered complaint, as in to grumble without open protest.

clue.text: Patriarch mostly consuming American food item

indicators.note: eating up something means taking it inside
most of the name, its last letter dropped

parts.note: Moses is a patriarch of the Hebrew Bible

explanation.surface: An old prophet eats some American dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: MOSE ('mostly' cutting the last letter of MOSES) takes in US.
explanation.definitionFit: A light whipped dessert, sweet or savoury.

clue.text: Show topless sister what she should be wearing

indicators.note: without its top, the first letter goes

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
a nun traditionally wears a veil

explanation.surface: A risque notice about a nun appearing without her top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first letter of NUN, leaving UN.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal or display something by removing its covering.

clue.text: Spot woman's instrument

parts.note: a zit is a pimple
her means belonging to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman's instrument has a blemish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot woman's instrument' reads like an order to spot it, but Spot is a pimple.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat stringed musical device plucked while resting on a table or lap.

clue.text: Fielding in the middle when over's unproductive

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are turned up, reading backwards
the central letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder in midfield finds the over a quiet one.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle four letters of FIELDING are ELDI, turned back by 'over'. An over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle hands or machines achieve nothing.

clue.text: Song about river, very old, is so long

indicators.note: the song is placed about, around, the other letters

parts.note: an air is a tune
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An old ballad about a river turns out to be a farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river; 'so long' reads as length but means goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: French farewell, used in English as goodbye until we meet again.

clue.text: University athlete on percussion instrument

annotationWithheld.why: University athlete on percussion instrument: BLUE is the athlete, but nothing gives MURDER and there is no definition; the clue appears cut short

clue.text: Particles in chains, lacking resistance

indicators.note: lacking something means it is missing from the word

parts.note: irons are fetters or chains
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Particles held in shackles, no longer resisting.
explanation.definitionFit: Charged atoms or molecules.
